question: Where does Promptus maintenance time go at MoT scale, and which hardware-agnostic software changes reduce work without weakening its integrity contract?

oneCpuExt4.caveat: The disposable snapshot contained two benchmark-only ledger events by this control; unit count was 5,340 rather than 5,338.

observed: The same full gate took 109.34 seconds on WSL 9p and 3.61 seconds on ext4; this storage contrast exposes metadata-heavy redundant traversal rather than defining a storage-specific solution.
A one-CPU ext4 control tracked the inherited-CPU ext4 timings, so the current hot path is not CPU-throughput limited.
Single-pass thinker binding preserved the exact binding count and digest and was faster on every profile: 10.75× on WSL 9p, 3.33× on ext4, and 3.17× on tmpfs.
Hashing each unique declared artifact path once preserved every verifier outcome and was faster on every profile: 1.62× on WSL 9p, 1.35× on ext4, and 1.53× on tmpfs.
inferred: The first optimization objective should be fewer source opens, parses, hashes, and derived writes per operation; elapsed time is the validation measure, not the architecture.

A full maintenance command should construct one immutable store snapshot and reuse it for source hashing, indexing, thinker custody, graph checks, and health reporting instead of rescanning between phases.
Global incremental indexing is a later step: exact single-pass traversal, dependency-aware refresh, path-deduplicated hashing, and batching are simpler and already supported by measured evidence.
GPU acceleration is irrelevant to this maintenance path; additional CPU cores will matter only after an explicitly bounded parallel phase exists.

engineeringSequence.change: Create one thinker exchange context: scan findings once, map quarantine IDs to bindings, reuse it for every round, refresh only when thinker inputs or findings change, and avoid rewriting identical derived files.
engineeringSequence.correctnessBoundary: Every round status, issue, binding, digest, ROUND.md, and INDEX.md must match the current implementation byte-for-byte.

engineeringSequence.change: Refactor full maintenance around one immutable StoreSnapshot that reads and parses each source file once and feeds source hashing, catalog, graph, search, thinker custody, and health checks.
engineeringSequence.correctnessBoundary: The snapshot is built under the store lock or proves its source generation stayed stable; derived outputs and health results must equal a clean full rebuild.

engineeringSequence.change: Deduplicate artifact content hashing by normalized real path while comparing the one digest against every historical artifact record that references it.
engineeringSequence.correctnessBoundary: The authoritative full gate remains exact; no stat-only cache may stand in for content hashing.

engineeringSequence.change: Add transactional batch kb-add so one lock, relation-resolution snapshot, dependency-aware refresh, and index serve a bounded set of writes.
engineeringSequence.correctnessBoundary: All-or-nothing source mutation, unique IDs, and a single authoritative post-batch receipt.

engineeringSequence.change: Add a clearly PARTIAL touched-files checkpoint and a writer-produced change receipt; develop a persistent incremental index only if the earlier work still misses the latency budget.
engineeringSequence.correctnessBoundary: A partial receipt can never masquerade as whole-store health; full rebuilds must converge byte-for-byte.

workConservationTargets.currentWaste: Refreshes all thinker rounds and repeatedly scans every finding even when a ledger event cannot affect thinker custody
workConservationTargets.targetWork: One source mutation, one catalog delta, zero finding-tree scans unless a declared thinker dependency changed
workConservationTargets.acceptance: Same unit bytes and ID; unrelated writes leave thinker derived bytes unchanged

workConservationTargets.currentWaste: Parses the store, then independently rescans findings for each thinker round
workConservationTargets.targetWork: Read and parse every source file at most once; derive catalog, graph, search, source hash, and thinker bindings from one snapshot
workConservationTargets.acceptance: All derived files are byte-for-byte equal to a clean reference rebuild

workConservationTargets.currentWaste: Runs the index, fingerprints the store again, reinspects thinker custody, and rehashes repeated artifact paths
workConservationTargets.targetWork: Reuse the index snapshot and hash each canonical artifact file once while checking every owning record
workConservationTargets.acceptance: Identical hard failures, archival warnings, graph debt, source hash, and final readiness

workConservationTargets.currentWaste: B writes repeat locks, relation collection, thinker refresh, and maintenance handoffs
workConservationTargets.targetWork: One lock and resolver snapshot for B all-or-nothing mutations, followed by one dependency-aware refresh and one index receipt
workConservationTargets.acceptance: Unique IDs, no lost events, rollback on any failed item, and full-rebuild convergence

workConservationTargets.currentWaste: A whole-store ratchet is the only strong receipt, so inner-loop bookkeeping pays global cost
workConservationTargets.targetWork: Verify the transaction's touched sources, relations, and new artifacts only
workConservationTargets.acceptance: Receipt is explicitly PARTIAL and cannot satisfy a full-gate requirement

hardwareGuidance.evidence: Single-pass thinker and unique-path artifact probes improved all three measured filesystems with exact-equivalent outputs
hardwareGuidance.design: Use the same work-conserving algorithms everywhere: one source snapshot, dependency-aware refresh, one hash per artifact path, and batched transactions.

hardwareGuidance.evidence: WSL 9p magnified redundant scans: 109.34 s full check and 38.90 s index
hardwareGuidance.design: Use this as the stress profile for file-open and traversal-count regressions, not as a reason for a platform-specific code path.

hardwareGuidance.evidence: ext4 full check was 3.61 s and tmpfs was 3.68 s
hardwareGuidance.design: Use as the overhead floor: reject optimizations whose cache bookkeeping makes the already-fast case slower or more complex without measured benefit.

hardwareGuidance.evidence: Observed full-check peak was 0.9 GiB on ext4
hardwareGuidance.design: Make source snapshots compact and stream derived serialization before adding parallelism; retain RSS and work counters in benchmark receipts.

hardwareGuidance.evidence: One-CPU ext4 timings were effectively unchanged; GPU was unused
hardwareGuidance.design: Do not require accelerators. Only consider a bounded artifact-hash worker pool after deduplication, with one-worker equivalence as the reference path.

methodology.isolation: All mutations and full maintenance trials ran against byte-matched snapshots; the live MoT store was read-only.
methodology.timing: GNU time wall/user/system/RSS receipts around unmodified Promptus commands plus benchmark-only phase probes.
methodology.repetitions: Fast operations used 2-5 repetitions and report the median. Expensive end-to-end operations used one repetition, corroborated by the operator's independent measurements and a live read-only doctor run.
methodology.cacheState: Snapshots were staged immediately before measurement, so results characterize a warm working session rather than cold-boot storage.
methodology.equivalence: Candidate thinker and artifact phases were accepted only after exact output digests/outcome counts matched current behavior.

limitations: The storage comparison uses one WSL2 host and one large project snapshot; it does not yet measure bare-metal Windows, macOS, NFS, SMB, or slower local disks.
Most expensive operations have n=1 because a complete WSL 9p suite is long; the independent operator timings are consistent but not a substitute for more hosts.
The single-pass thinker and unique-path artifact measurements are isolated prototypes, not implemented end-to-end Promptus patches.
The one-CPU control followed two disposable benchmark writes, a 0.04% unit-count difference; use it as a bottleneck classification control, not an exact release benchmark.
